description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
- Fixed: **sorting by a number with decimals is right on any server, whatever its language
        settings.** On a machine set to a culture that writes decimals with a comma, such as Norwegian or
        German, a sort by a decimal field (a price, a rating) came out in the wrong order with no error:
        values were read with that culture rather than as JSON numbers. A document without the value now
        sorts last in both directions, as documented, where it used to sort as 0.
      - Changed: **Insert and Update refuse a document with a field the field configuration does not
        know**, and name it: `InsertJsonRecord(s)` and `UpdateJsonRecord(s)` return `false` with
        "... the document has field(s) not in the field configuration: 'color'" (nested fields by path,
        `'meta.batch'`). They used to succeed and store the field, which was then never indexed,
        searched or filtered, and could not be configured afterwards - a silent no-op. A batch with one
        such record changes nothing, and an Update leaves the document as it was. To bring in a new
        field, analyse again: a new `Init` and `Load` (on the server, a replace). Over HTTP the refusal
        is `400 invalidArgument` with the same message.
      - Added: **a reason for every `false`** on the methods that had none. `LoadFieldConfiguration`,
        `SaveFieldConfiguration`, `LoadSynonyms`, `SaveSynonyms`, `WakeUp` and `LoadFilters` each gain
        an overload with `out string error` saying why (file missing, unreadable, wrong state, nothing
        to save, a failed rebuild). The existing signatures are unchanged and delegate to them.
      - Added: **`TrySetFieldConfiguration(fields, out string error)`**, returning `true` on success
        like its neighbours. `SetFieldConfiguration`, the one member of the surface where `null` meant
        success, is now `[Obsolete]`; it still behaves exactly as before, so existing code compiles
        with a warning that names the replacement.
      - Fixed: **`WakeUp` returns `false` when the wake did not succeed.** It returned `true` as soon as
        the index build and the filter load had finished, whether or not they had worked, so a failed
        rebuild read as a successful wake. A wake whose filter indexes failed to build reports the
        failure even though the engine is searchable, since the call did not do everything it was asked.
      - Fixed: **a filter load that throws is reported, not passed off as success.** `LoadAllFilters`
        marked its monitor `Succeeded` even when the load threw; it now carries the error and the
        exception. `LoadFilters` returns `false` with the reason instead of throwing.
      - Fixed: **a vector that arrives after `Index()` now reaches the embedding index.** Since
        5.0.0-RC260926 a document inserted with `InsertJsonRecord(s)` or replaced with
        `UpdateJsonRecord(s)` was stored with its vector but was not findable by vector or hybrid
        search until the next full `Load`; `UpdateField` on the vector field removed the document from
        vector search altogether; and `CreateInMemoryClone` dropped the vector of any document inserted
        after `Index()`. Documents that came in through `Load` were never affected. The cause was that
        the set of fields a document is parsed with did not include embeddable fields on those paths,
        which stopped mattering only when array values became stored for fields in use alone. No API
        change.
      - Fixed: **`UpdateField` takes every numeric type it validates.** A `float`, `decimal`, `short`
        or unsigned value - and so a `float[]` vector - passed validation and was then refused as
        "invalid primitive data type". And a `null` element in an array value was stored as the
        number `7`; it is now stored as `null`.
      - Removed **`SystemState.Hibernated (-1)`**. Hibernation is no longer a state of its own but a
        step backwards along the lifecycle: `Hibernate()` frees the index and search pools, keeps the
        documents in memory, and lands in **`Loaded`** — which is factually what the engine then is.
        `WakeUp()` stays as the convenience transition out of `Loaded` (`Index()` plus filter
        reload); its guard accordingly changed from "requires Hibernated" to "requires Loaded", so it
        now also works on a freshly loaded, never-indexed engine. `Unload()` is unchanged: deep sleep,
        back to `Created`. A `switch` over `SystemState` with a `Hibernated` arm is a compile error
        whose fix is deleting the arm; code comparing the numeric `-1` should compare against `Loaded`
        instead.
title: IndxSearchLib
